quests.instruction: Why is it unsafe to lean back on two legs of a chair?
quests.correctAnswer: The chair can tip over 🪑
options: The legs can wear out 🔧
The floor can get dusty 🧹
The chair can tip over 🪑
quests.hint: Ask yourself what keeps a chair steady.
quests.explanation: A chair is balanced on four legs. Tipping it onto two makes it easy to fall backward and hit your head.
quests.funFact: Chairs are designed to carry weight straight down through all four legs.

quests.instruction: Grandpa has sore knees. Which seat is easiest for him to get up from?
quests.correctAnswer: A firm chair with arms 🪑
options: A low, squashy beanbag 🫘
A firm chair with arms 🪑
A cushion on the floor 🧘
quests.hint: He needs height and something to push against.
quests.explanation: A higher, firm seat with arms gives you something to push on when standing. Low, soft seats make standing up much harder.
quests.funFact: Seats that are tall enough for knees to stay bent only a little are easiest for many older people.

quests.instruction: A toddler joins the family at the dinner table. What helps them sit safely?
quests.correctAnswer: A booster seat or high chair 🪑
options: A stack of heavy books 📚
A booster seat or high chair 🪑
A wobbly little kitchen stool 🪜
quests.hint: Choose something built to stay put and hold a small child.
quests.explanation: A booster seat or high chair raises a small child safely to table height and stays steady. Books slide and stools can tip.
quests.funFact: Many high chairs have a strap to keep a young child from slipping out.

quests.instruction: Which table usually sits in front of a sofa, holding books and cups?
quests.correctAnswer: A coffee table ☕
options: A coffee table ☕
A bedside table 🌙
A dining table 🍽️
quests.hint: Look for the table that sits beside a sofa, not a bed or a dining room.
quests.explanation: A coffee table sits in the living area, low enough to reach from a sofa. A bedside table is beside a bed, and a dining table is for meals.
quests.funFact: Some coffee tables have a shelf underneath for magazines or remote controls.

quests.instruction: Why should you not stand or sit on a coffee table?
quests.correctAnswer: It may not be built to hold you ⚠️
options: It has to stay perfectly clean and shiny ✨
It may not be built to hold you ⚠️
It is too small for anyone to see 🔍
quests.hint: Work out what the table was designed to carry.
quests.explanation: Tables are made to hold things, not people. A table can break or tip and someone could be hurt.
quests.funFact: Some tables are made from glass, which can crack under weight.

quests.instruction: One leg of the table feels wobbly. What should a child do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell a grown-up so it can be fixed 🧑
options: Tell a grown-up so it can be fixed 🧑
Lean on it to test it 💪
Prop it with a pile of plates 🍽️
quests.hint: A fix needs tools and an adult who knows how.
quests.explanation: A wobbly table can tip and spill things. A grown-up can tighten it or fix the leg. Plates stacked under it would slide and break.
quests.funFact: A folded piece of paper is sometimes used as a short-term wedge, but only as a temporary fix.

quests.instruction: A big sister and a little brother want to play the same game. Which choice is fairest?
quests.correctAnswer: Change the rules so both can join 🤝
options: Let the big sister always win 🏆
Play the game without the little brother 🚪
Change the rules so both can join 🤝
quests.hint: Fair games are ones where everyone can take part.
quests.explanation: Changing the rules a little lets everyone join in and enjoy it. Always winning or leaving someone out is not fair.
quests.funFact: Teams often give younger players a head start to make a game more even.

quests.instruction: The show is over, but a younger child wants another one. How can the family decide fairly?
quests.correctAnswer: Take turns choosing the show 🔄
options: Take turns choosing the show 🔄
Let the loudest voice decide 📢
Always let the oldest pick 🧑
quests.hint: A fair plan gives everybody a chance.
quests.explanation: Taking turns gives each person a fair chance to pick. The loudest or the oldest should not always decide.
quests.funFact: A list on the fridge can remember whose turn it is.

quests.instruction: The baby is napping in the next room. Which quiet family activity fits?
quests.correctAnswer: Reading or drawing together 📖
options: A loud game with a toy drum 🥁
A jumping contest on the sofa 🤸
Reading or drawing together 📖
quests.hint: Choose something that makes little noise.
quests.explanation: Quiet activities let everyone enjoy time together without waking the baby. Drums and jumping are too loud.
quests.funFact: Babies often nap in short blocks, so quiet time may not last very long.

quests.instruction: A dish is far away from you at the table. What is the polite thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask someone to pass it 🙏
options: Stand on your chair to reach 🪑
Ask someone to pass it 🙏
Reach across other people's plates ✋
quests.hint: Using your voice is safer than using your arm.
quests.explanation: Asking someone to pass a dish is polite and safe. Standing on chairs or reaching across plates can knock things over.
quests.funFact: 'Please pass the...' is a way of asking for something at the table that people use around the world.

quests.instruction: You do not like the vegetable on your plate. What is the polite thing to say?
quests.correctAnswer: I'll try a small piece, please 🥦
options: I'll try a small piece, please 🥦
That looks disgusting 🤢
I will throw this under the table 🗑️
quests.hint: Be honest, kind, and willing.
quests.explanation: Trying a small piece is kind to the cook, and it helps you find out what you like. Rude words or hiding food is not polite.
quests.funFact: People often need to try a new food several times before they enjoy it.

quests.instruction: Why do many families keep phones away from the table during meals?
quests.correctAnswer: So everyone can talk together 💬
options: Because phones do not fit on tables 📱
So everyone can talk together 💬
Because phones can spoil the plates 🍽️
quests.hint: Meals are a time for faces, not screens.
quests.explanation: Putting phones aside lets people listen to each other and enjoy the food. Meals are one of the few times a whole family is together.
quests.funFact: A basket for phones by the door can keep them out of sight until dinner is over.

quests.instruction: A guest your family invited arrives. What is a friendly thing to do first?
quests.correctAnswer: Greet them and show where coats go 🧥
options: Greet them and show where coats go 🧥
Ignore them completely 🙈
Tell them to wait outside for a while 🚪
quests.hint: A welcome starts with a hello.
quests.explanation: A friendly greeting makes guests feel welcome, and showing them where to put their coat is helpful. Ignoring or leaving them outside is unwelcoming.
quests.funFact: In many places guests are offered something to drink soon after they arrive.

quests.instruction: A visitor does not eat meat. How can the family help?
quests.correctAnswer: Offer a meal without meat 🥗
options: Make them eat the meat anyway 🍖
Tell them to eat at home first 🏠
Offer a meal without meat 🥗
quests.hint: A good host thinks about what the guest can enjoy.
quests.explanation: Offering food they can eat shows care. Pushing food on someone who can't or won't eat it is not kind.
quests.funFact: People avoid certain foods for many reasons, including beliefs, health, or taste.

quests.instruction: Where is a good place to offer a guest a seat?
quests.correctAnswer: A sofa or a table chair 🛋️
options: The floor beside the front door 🚪
A sofa or a table chair 🛋️
The stairs in the front hallway 🪜
quests.hint: Consider where a visitor would be comfortable.
quests.explanation: A guest should have a comfortable seat. A floor by the door or the stairs is in the way and less welcoming.
quests.funFact: Many homes keep an extra folding chair for when more guests come.

quests.instruction: After movie night the living room has cups, a blanket, and popcorn on the floor. Which job should go first?
quests.correctAnswer: Take cups and trash to the kitchen 🥤
options: Take cups and trash to the kitchen 🥤
Fold the blanket up neatly 🧶
Fluff up all the cushions 🛋️
quests.hint: Start with what might spill, stain, or attract bugs.
quests.explanation: Cups and food trash can spill and attract insects, so they go first. Folding and fluffing are the finishing touches.
quests.funFact: A small bin near the sofa makes movie-night clean-up quicker.

quests.instruction: Where should the remote control live so that everybody can find it?
quests.correctAnswer: In one spot, like a tray 📺
options: In one spot, like a tray 📺
Wherever it was last dropped ❓
Inside a sofa cushion cover 🛋️
quests.hint: A fixed home means no searching.
quests.explanation: A regular spot means anybody can find the remote right away. Wherever it was dropped makes everyone search.
quests.funFact: Small trays or baskets keep remotes together in one spot.

quests.instruction: Why is it better to put books and toys away after using the living room?
quests.correctAnswer: Others can use the space 🛋️
options: The floor looks more colorful and fun 🎨
Others can use the space 🛋️
The toys can rest on a high shelf 🧸
quests.hint: A shared space belongs to everybody.
quests.explanation: A living room is shared, so putting things away leaves it ready for the next person and keeps walkways clear.
quests.funFact: A quick two-minute tidy before dinner can reset a shared room.

quests.instruction: Dad is on a work call in the living room. What is the most considerate choice for a child?
quests.correctAnswer: Play quietly or in another room 🤫
options: Turn up the music louder 🎵
Play quietly or in another room 🤫
Run laps around the whole sofa 🏃
quests.hint: Ask yourself what he can hear.
quests.explanation: Playing quietly or moving to another room lets him hear and be heard. Loud music and running would be hard to talk over.
quests.funFact: Headphones let people share a room without hearing each other's music.

quests.instruction: Two siblings both want the big armchair at the same moment. What is a fair solution?
quests.correctAnswer: Take turns or share the space 🔄
options: The bigger one always gets it 💪
Whoever sits first keeps it forever ⏰
Take turns or share the space 🔄
quests.hint: A fair plan works for both people.
quests.explanation: Taking turns or squeezing in together gives both a fair go. Winning by size or speed means the other always loses.
quests.funFact: Some armchairs are wide enough for two small people.

quests.instruction: How can you ask a family member to turn the TV down?
quests.correctAnswer: Politely ask them to lower it 🗣️
options: Unplug it without warning 🔌
Shout louder than the TV does 📢
Politely ask them to lower it 🗣️
quests.hint: Kind words work better than surprises.
quests.explanation: Asking politely gets results without upsetting anyone. Unplugging or shouting causes arguments.
quests.funFact: Most TVs have a volume button on the remote that makes adjusting easy.

quests.instruction: Which spot is best for a family meeting to plan the week?
quests.correctAnswer: Around the dining table 🍽️
options: In the family bathroom 🛁
Around the dining table 🍽️
Standing along the hallway 🚶
quests.hint: Pick a spot where everybody can sit, see each other, and put a calendar down.
quests.explanation: A table gives everyone a seat facing each other and a flat spot for a calendar. A bathroom or hallway is too small and noisy.
quests.funFact: A shared calendar helps families remember who needs to be where.

quests.instruction: Which activity is better at a dining table than on a living-room sofa?
quests.correctAnswer: Crafts needing a flat table ✂️
options: Taking a quick afternoon nap 😴
Crafts needing a flat table ✂️
Watching a favorite movie show 📺
quests.hint: Consider what each piece of furniture is built for.
quests.explanation: Crafts need a flat, steady surface, which a table gives. A sofa is better for napping or watching a screen.
quests.funFact: Craft mats or old newspaper protect a table while you work.

quests.instruction: In a one-room flat the table is used for meals and homework. How can both jobs work?
quests.correctAnswer: Clear one job away first 🧹
options: Clear one job away first 🧹
Do both jobs at exactly the same time 🍽️
Never use the table for anything 🚫
quests.hint: A shared surface can only do one job at a time.
quests.explanation: Clearing the table between jobs keeps food off the books and schoolwork away from the meal. One table can serve many purposes if each gets its turn.
quests.funFact: Many small homes use a basket to tidy homework quickly before dinner.

quests.instruction: A family expects eight guests for lunch. What should they plan first?
quests.correctAnswer: Where everyone will sit 🪑
options: Where everyone will sit 🪑
Which songs to play 🎵
What color the napkins are 🎨
quests.hint: Start with what everybody needs.
quests.explanation: Seating is the first need, since everyone has to eat comfortably. Music and decorations come after the basics.
quests.funFact: Folding chairs, benches, and cushions are useful extras.

quests.instruction: How can you make the living room safer before a big gathering?
quests.correctAnswer: Move toys and cords from walkways 🧸
options: Add more furniture to the walkway 🛋️
Turn off the lights to save power 💡
Move toys and cords from walkways 🧸
quests.hint: More people means more walking, and more chances to trip.
quests.explanation: Clear paths let many people move safely. More furniture or dim lights make tripping more likely.
quests.funFact: A good rule is to leave a clear path wide enough for two people to pass.

quests.instruction: One guest cannot eat nuts. What should the family do about the snacks?
quests.correctAnswer: Choose nut-free snacks and check labels 🥜
options: Hope the guest will avoid them 🙏
Put nuts in everything on the table 🌰
Choose nut-free snacks and check labels 🥜
quests.hint: Check what is in the food before putting it out.
quests.explanation: Reading labels and picking nut-free snacks keeps a guest safe. Guessing is risky, and for some people even a little can cause a serious reaction.
quests.funFact: Many snack packages list common allergens near the ingredients.

quests.instruction: Three people want the living room at once: one for TV, one to read, one to nap. What is the best solution?
quests.correctAnswer: Plan it, with headphones for TV 🎧
options: Plan it, with headphones for TV 🎧
Shout to decide who wins 📢
Let one person decide it all 👑
quests.hint: Think about how to share without anyone losing.
quests.explanation: Planning together lets each person get what they need, and headphones keep the TV from bothering the others.
quests.funFact: Sharing a room is easier when everyone knows the rules ahead of time.

quests.instruction: A guest accidentally spills juice on the sofa. What is the kind response?
quests.correctAnswer: Say it is okay and help clean up 🧽
options: Look angry and say nothing at all 😠
Ask the guest to go home 🚪
Say it is okay and help clean up 🧽
quests.hint: Accidents happen to everyone.
quests.explanation: Staying kind and helping clean up shows good manners, and sofas can be cleaned. Anger or sending someone away makes things worse.
quests.funFact: Blotting a spill, not rubbing it, helps keep it from spreading into the fabric.

quests.instruction: Which sentence best describes a well-run shared space?
quests.correctAnswer: Things have homes, all help 🧺
options: One person does all of the work 👑
There are no rules for anyone 🚫
Things have homes, all help 🧺
quests.hint: Think about how a group keeps a space pleasant.
quests.explanation: When things have homes and everyone helps, the space stays tidy and comfortable. One person doing everything or having no rules is not fair or workable.
quests.funFact: Even small jobs, done by everyone, add up to a big difference.
